chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabalah and Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from Jameel from Ismail al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

Five [types of women] can be divorced in every state: the pregnant, the one from whom her husband is absent, the one who has not yet menstruated, the one who has despaired of menstruation, and the one who has not been entered into (consummated).
Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jameel from Ismail al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), similar to it.
ai.seo_question: Which five types of women can be divorced at any time according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the general prohibition against divorcing women during their menstrual period (Surah At-Talaq) does not apply to these five specific categories, allowing for immediate divorce (talaq al-sunnah or talaq al-kharij) without the need for a waiting period tied to menstruation. This ruling is significant in Shia fiqh for resolving cases where the standard iddah conditions are inapplicable, such as in pre-puberty or post-menopause scenarios, ensuring legal clarity for marital dissolution.
